key_insight: A self-supervised functional autoencoder learns a reusable latent space, separating function representation from task-specific neural operator training.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics surrogates, frozen representations can reduce training memory and accelerate inference while supporting fields sampled on arbitrary point clouds.
method: Pre-train on analytic functions synthesized without PDE solvers or labels.
Freeze translation-, dilation-, and amplitude-equivariant representation maps and cache dataset embeddings.
Train task-specific operators in latent space and decode predicted fields.
evidence_signal: Across 28 tasks spanning solid mechanics, fluids, acoustics, Helmholtz, and Poisson equations, the abstract reports accuracy that can exceed state-of-the-art end-to-end models, with up to an order-of-magnitude throughput gain.
watch_item: Transfer to a specific mechanics application still requires validation; the abstract does not establish accuracy guarantees or physical constraint satisfaction.
paper_title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
